newsitem.title: USA: FUND VIEW - Gold funds lack luster.
newsitem.headline: FUND VIEW - Gold funds lack luster.

text.p: Investors in gold funds have consistently pulled money out of the group in recent weeks, as the sector has suffered from chronic lackluster performance.

The natural resources -- or gold -- sector had net redemptions totalling $25 million for the week ended April 30, the seventh consecutive week of outflows, according to Robert Adler, president of AMG Data Services of Arcata, Calif. For the previous week, redemptions were $15 million.
Carl Wittnebert, director of research at Mutual Fund Trim Tabs, said the net asset value of six gold funds it follows fell by 7.5 percent for the month of April.
Adler traced the redemptions to the Busang saga at Bre-X Minerals Ltd's "This clearly was off with the Bre-X issue," said Adler.

Bre-X stock has been driven down since March, after doubt was cast on a gold find at the Busang project in Indonesia. Bre-X had called it biggest find of this century, then said there was a strong possibility that the potential resources were overstated.
Bre-X shares rose C$0.23 to C$3.27 on Friday, after trading as high as C$28.65 earlier this year.
Gold suffered a general decline last month. Spot gold prices fell steadily in April to a low around $337.50 an ounce, revisiting the four year lows seen in January.

Sales of gold reserves by European central banks, ahead of the introduction of European Monetary Union (EMU) in 1999, have depressed the gold market in the past year, after gold prices hit a six-year high around $417 an ounce in January last year.
There has also been little need for gold as an inflation hedge. Also, a soaring stock market in the past year has proved more attractive for investors.
As a result, fund portfolios have been under pressure, said Michael Lipper, president of Lipper Analytical Services.

The Lipper Gold Fund Index fell 0.12 percent for the week ended May 1, and was down 14.37 percent year to date. For the past year, the index has lost 28.48 percent, but has returned 37.01 percent over the past five years. The index is comprised of 10 of the largest of the 49 open-end gold funds.
Lipper said that among the worst weekly trailing funds were Lexington Strategic Investments, down 3.35 percent; Gabelli Gold, off 2.52 percent, and Fidelity Select Precious Metals, down 2.07 percent.
Equity funds overall had inflows of $2.9 billion versus $2.5 billion for the week of April 23, and $4.5 billion for the same week a year ago.
"Clearly, flows were heavy into speculative funds a year ago, and we're not seeing that dramatic jump now," said Adler.

Among other stock fund sectors, the month-long strength of flows into the international sector continued for the week ended April 30, with $631 million in inflows compared to $615 million for the previous week.
Adler noted that growth and income funds saw a decline in flows to $896 million for the week, down from $1.1 billion the previous week.

According to AMG, two funds captured a big chunk of the money going into the growth and income sector for the week: Vanguard Institutional Index fund at $245 million, and Fidelty Growth and Income at $70 million.
